definition: Lack of success; the opposite of the movement's destiny as she named it.
example: Failure is impossible.

definition: Not able to occur or be done—except when she denied the word power.
example: Failure is impossible.

definition: A system or act of voting; the paper or ticket used to cast a vote.
example: It was we, the people; not we, the white male citizens; nor yet we, the male citizens; but we, the whole people, who formed the Union—and the ballot belongs to that whole.

definition: A legally recognized member of a state with rights and duties.
example: It was we, the people; not we, the white male citizens; nor yet we, the male citizens; but we, the whole people, who formed the Union.

definition: The United States as a political whole; a joining into one body.
example: It was we, the people; not we, the white male citizens; nor yet we, the male citizens; but we, the whole people, who formed the Union.

definition: Government by a small privileged group.
example: To them this government is not a democracy; it is not a republic; it is an odious aristocracy; a hateful oligarchy of sex.

definition: Rule by a hereditary or elite class.
example: To them this government is not a democracy; it is not a republic; it is an odious aristocracy; a hateful oligarchy of sex.

definition: Extremely unpleasant; deserving hatred.
example: To them this government is not a democracy; it is not a republic; it is an odious aristocracy; a hateful oligarchy of sex.

definition: The right to vote in political elections.
example: Suffrage is the pivotal right.

definition: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something.
example: Suffrage is the pivotal right.

definition: Freedom from control by others; self-government.
example: Cautious, careful people, always casting about to preserve their reputation and social standing, never can bring about a reform—independence of mind is required.

definition: Make changes in order to improve a system or institution.
example: Cautious, careful people, always casting about to preserve their reputation and social standing, never can bring about a reform.

definition: Coordinate people into an effective body for action.
example: The true woman will not be exponent of another, or allow another to be such for her—she will organize her own power.

definition: Seize by legal authority and take into custody.
example: I was arrested for voting, and I am as guilty of the crime of demanding my rights as any freeman who ever cast a ballot.

definition: Responsible for a specified wrong—or proudly so in civil disobedience.
example: I shall earnestly and persistently continue to urge all women to the practical recognition of the old revolutionary maxim that Resistance to tyranny is obedience to God—and if that makes me guilty, so be it.

definition: Cruel and oppressive government or rule.
example: Resistance to tyranny is obedience to God.

definition: The opening statement of a constitution that declares its purpose.
example: The preamble of the Federal Constitution says: We, the people of the United States, in order to form a more perfect union.

definition: Calm and public peace — the Constitution's own spelling of the aim.
example: We, the people of the United States, in order to form a more perfect union, establish justice, insure domestic tranquillity.

definition: A formal accusation of a crime.
example: I stand before you tonight under indictment for the alleged crime of having voted at the last presidential election.

definition: All future generations.
example: The preamble secures the blessings of liberty to ourselves and our posterity — and she asked who was missing from that we.

definition: To admit to the rights of citizenship, especially the vote.
example: To enfranchise women, she argued, was not a favor. It was what We, the people already required.

definition: Contrary to the constitution.
example: A republic that taxes a woman and bars her vote is, by its own preamble, unconstitutional in spirit.

definition: The body of people entitled to vote.
example: The electorate she demanded was the people, not the male half of the people.

definition: To take away the right to vote.
example: Laws that disenfranchise half the nation cannot claim the name of a republic.

definition: The legal process of becoming a citizen.
example: She asked whether naturalization and citizenship were real if the vote that defines them was closed to her.

definition: Open resistance to a government.
example: Resistance to tyranny is obedience to God, she reminded them, and their fathers had once called that rebellion.
